candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the names of entries inside a ZIP archive that the application extracts (e.g. an uploaded/downloaded archive, a build artifact, or any file obtained from an untrusted source). Entry names can contain '../' sequences (and '..\' when BackslashUnpacker is used); Java's ZipFile/ZipInputStream expose these names verbatim via ZipEntry.getName().
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked the caller-specified-destination overloads doUnpackEntry(ZipFile, String, File) (ZipUtil.java:389-417) and unpackEntry(..., File) (318-434): the entry name is only used for ZipFile.getEntry lookup and the target file is supplied by the caller, so those overloads are not affected. Searched the whole tree for '..', 'canonical', 'normalize', 'startsWith', 'getCanonicalPath', and traversal/slip guards - the extraction code contains none; ZipUtil only has a startsWith check in filterDirEntries (2368) for removal filtering, unrelated to extraction. Confirmed IdentityNameMapper returns names unchanged and ZipEntryOrInfoAdapter does not rewrite names. Confirmed FileUtils.copy writes to FileOutputStream without re-resolving or validating the path. Note: on Unix a purely absolute entry name is normally folded under the destination by the File(File,String) constructor, so the practical vectors are '../' segments (and '..\'/drive-relative names on Windows, especially through BackslashUnpacker) - this does not weaken the finding.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation or overwrite outside the intended extraction directory, with the privileges of the extracting process. Depending on deployment this can overwrite application configuration or code, shell profiles/cron entries, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, or web-served content, leading to code execution or privilege abuse. The extraction loops also continue after the write, so traversal entries are silent and the archive still unpacks normally.
candidates.prerequisites: The application calls one of the public extraction APIs on an untrusted archive: ZipUtil.unpack(File|InputStream, File[, NameMapper][, Charset]), ZipUtil.unwrap(...), ZipUtil.explode(File), or Zips.get(src).destination(dir)/unpack().process(); the extracting process must have write permission to a path outside the chosen destination; no application-supplied NameMapper sanitizes names (default usage does not).
candidates.root_cause: All whole-archive extraction callbacks join the ZIP entry name to the caller-supplied output directory with new File(outputDir, name) (or new File(destination, entryName)) and then write with FileUtils.copy/FileOutputStream, without ever checking that the resolved path remains inside the destination. No normalization, '..' rejection, absolute-path handling, or canonical-path containment check exists anywhere in the extraction path; the default IdentityNameMapper even returns the raw entry name.
candidates.title: Zip Slip: archive-controlled entry names are written outside the extraction directory
candidates.trace: ZipEntry.getName() -> Unpacker.process (ZipUtil.java:1150) / Unwraper.process (1258) / BackslashUnpacker.process (1196, 1208-1225) / Zips.UnpackingCallback.process (Zips.java:676) -> mapper.map() returns the name unchanged by default -> new File(outputDir, name) (ZipUtil.java:1152, 1220, 1225, 1260) or new File(destination, entryName) (Zips.java:683) -> FileUtils.forceMkdir(parent)/createNewFile -> FileUtils.copy(InputStream, File) (commons/FileUtils.java:53-61) opens FileOutputStream on the OS-resolved path, so '..' segments escape the destination; no check occurs between the join and the write.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and the snapshot contains no test sources, so the traversal was not demonstrated at runtime; exploitability depends on the consuming application actually passing an untrusted archive to these APIs, which cannot be observed from this repository. The repository-provided version (1.13-SNAPSHOT) is consistent with a pre-fix revision, but fix history was not consulted (out of scope).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Zip Slip) / path traversal

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded decompression / zip bomb: FileUtils.copy and IOUtils.copy (4 KB loop) impose no entry size, total size, or compression-ratio limits.
rejected_leads.reason: Real but availability-only and generic to decompressors; no repository-specific evidence of a stronger consequence than resource exhaustion, so it is weaker than the traversal candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: AsiExtraField.parseFromLocalFileData (extra/AsiExtraField.java:369-401) with a declared ASi (0x756E) extra-field length < 4 triggers NegativeArraySizeException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (via new byte[length-WORD] / ZipShort.getValue(tmp,0)); reachable when getZTFilePermissions parses crafted extra data.
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker-controllable crash/exception (availability only), and the parse entry point in ExtraFieldUtils.parse does validate the overall block bounds; lower impact than arbitrary file write.

rejected_leads.lead: ZTFilePermissionsUtil applies permissions/mode bits taken from the archive to extracted files (ZipEntryUtil.getZTFilePermissions:190-204; Java6/Java7 permission strategies), potentially producing executable or world-writable files.
rejected_leads.reason: Hardening concern rather than a distinct exploit path; requires the application to extract into a sensitive location and is not independently exploitable in the source shown.

rejected_leads.lead: Symlink-following writes: FileUtils.copy uses FileOutputStream and Java7Nio2ApiPermissionsStrategy sets permissions on paths that could be pre-existing symlinks inside the destination directory.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an attacker to place symlinks in the destination beforehand; speculative and not demonstrated by source evidence.

summary: The snapshot is zt-zip 1.13-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml:8; Changelog tops out at 1.12), a ZIP manipulation library. Its whole-archive extraction APIs build destination paths directly from archive-controlled entry names without any containment check, i.e. classic Zip Slip / CWE-22 path traversal: ZipUtil.unpack*/unwrap/explode (ZipUtil.Unpacker, Unwraper, BackslashUnpacker) and the Zips fluent API (Zips.UnpackingCallback) all do new File(outputDir, name) / new File(destination, entryName) and then FileUtils.forceMkdir(...parent) + FileUtils.copy(in, file). Nothing in the extraction path rejects ".." segments, absolute names, or otherwise verifies the resolved path stays under the destination (searches for "..", "canonical", "normalize", containment/startsWith checks found no guard; IdentityNameMapper passes names through unchanged). An archive with an entry such as "../../..." causes file creation/overwrite outside the chosen output directory with the extracting process's privileges. This is the single strongest issue; other observations (unbounded decompression, unchecked exceptions from ASi extra-field parsing, permission bits applied from archive metadata) are weaker and are listed as rejected leads rather than additional candidates.
